decision.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee lowered its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed reduced the benchmark interest rate to support economic activity.

changes.quote: In a related action, the Board of Governors approved a 25 basis point reduction in the discount rate to 2 percent.
changes.explanation: The direct lending rate for banks was also lowered.

changes.quote: Recent signs point to a firming in spending, markedly improved financial conditions, and labor and product markets that are stabilizing.
changes.explanation: The Committee noted early signs of stabilization in spending and markets.

changes.quote: The economy, nonetheless, has yet to exhibit sustainable growth.
changes.explanation: Despite stabilizing signs, the Fed wants to see stronger, sustained growth.

changes.quote: President Parry preferred a 50 basis point reduction in the target for the federal funds rate.
changes.explanation: One member dissented because they wanted a larger rate cut of 50 basis points.

tone_quotes.quote: With inflationary expectations subdued, the Committee judged that a slightly more expansive monetary policy would add further support for an economy which it expects to improve over time.
On balance, the Committee believes that the latter concern is likely to predominate for the foreseeable future.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.26% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.38% and moved +9 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.21% would rise by about $16.73 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 6.1%, and employers added an average of -81k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.9% over the past year (May 2003); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +16 bp on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve remains cautious about the pace of the economic recovery. Future policy decisions will depend on how economic data evolves regarding inflation and growth.
